clinician.trajectory_summary: A 40-year-old male presented with a 5-year history of hematospermia, painful ejaculation, and perineal discomfort. Initial evaluation showed negative urine culture, normal PSA, normal prostate ultrasound, and normal cystoscopy. Pelvic MRI revealed asymmetric seminal vesicles with an enlarged left seminal vesicle likely due to hematic content and identified a 7 mm lithiasic focus in the prostatoseminal angle, demonstrating the presence of seminal vesicle calculi. No further imaging or procedural results were available, but this MRI finding is the key diagnostic evidence supporting the diagnosis.
